sections.heading: Early responsibilities
sections.content: Figma’s first designer advocate was a passionate user who worked full-time with Claire Butler. He met with users, talked with them, wrote and created content, and brought what he learned back to the product. The role connected Figma with its design community and helped inform the product.

sections.heading: How the role supported go-to-market
sections.content: As the function scaled, advocates helped Figma build authentic relationships and credibility: they gut-checked marketing, helped pitch the company, and gathered feedback from people in the community. They also joined user conversations and sales calls as technical experts who could explain how the product addressed designers’ problems and suggest best practices. They were not salespeople and did not have sales quotas.

sections.content: The first designer advocate was a passionate user hired full-time to represent Figma: meeting and talking with users, writing and creating content, and bringing what they learned back to the product. Because the role deeply understood the tool and its users, the advocate could synthesize product feedback for the product team.

sections.heading: How the role supported go-to-market
sections.content: The advocate helped build credibility with designers and supported marketing and sales. In sales conversations, the advocate was a technical expert—not a salesperson, with no quota—who explained the product, understood designers’ problems and blockers, and offered ideas or best practices for using it.
